findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the Pass-1 rubric severity-guidance sentence with a mechanism that actually gates priority: either (a) add severity-axis guidance to the T10 verifier prompt (which does emit severity_attributes that impact_plan reads), or (b) add an explicit per-class impact cap in a T10-specific impact_fn, or (c) accept that non-major T10 findings may block at 0.90 and remove the scoping claim from the Approach.
evidence: plan_review_finder.md line 21: 'Do NOT emit severity, confidence, or priority — a separate pass computes those'
decide.py lines 557-558: 'priority = round(val * imp, 4)' then 'sev = severity_label(imp)' — severity is computed AFTER priority, not before
decide.py line 588: blocking condition is 'blocking_enabled and priority >= block_threshold' — severity label is not in the blocking predicate
verify_models.py lines 217-275: the Pass-2 verifier emits severity_attributes ordinal axes that impact_plan() reads to compute impact; the Pass-1 finder emits no such axes

ABSENCE: no mechanism in the pipeline for the Pass-1 rubric to communicate 'this is a minor T10 class' to the Pass-2 verifier's severity_attributes, so the scoping sentence cannot influence the impact->priority computation
findings.finding: The plan's T10 class-scoping mechanism — 'one sentence added to plan_review_T10.md stating that only MAJOR classes warrant severity >= major so lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 priority threshold through the existing severity->priority pipeline' — names a protocol (severity gates priority) that does not match the actual pipeline. Pass-1 finders are explicitly prohibited from emitting severity; severity_label() is computed from impact AFTER priority (priority = validity × impact) is already determined. The only mechanism that controls priority is the Pass-2 verifier's severity_attributes ordinal axes consumed by impact_plan(). A rubric sentence directing the Pass-1 agent about 'MAJOR class' severity has no path to cap impact_plan()'s output.
findings.location: Approach section, step (2): 'one sentence added to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T10.md stating that only its MAJOR classes … warrant severity >= major — so lesser findings cannot reach the 0.90 priority threshold through the existing severity->priority pipeline'
scenarios: A T10 finding on a non-major class (e.g. cost/sizing or observability gap) where Pass-2 verifier grades severity_attributes axes as medium/high independently — the finding reaches priority ≥ 0.90 and blocks despite the rubric sentence designating it non-major, because the Pass-1 rubric has no influence over the Pass-2 verifier's ordinal axes.
The rubric sentence is present and checked by AC3, giving false confidence the scoping works, while the actual pipeline ignores it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the T10 DET regex intentionally duplicates T14 vocabulary ('.github/workflows', 'workflow_dispatch', 'pull_request_target', 'oidc', 'docker-compose', 'github actions', 'secrets\.[A-Z_]+') or whether those terms can be removed from T10 in favour of a tighter IaC-specific vocabulary (terraform/cloudformation/pulumi/ansible/kubernetes/iac/aws/ec2/s3/iam/ssm/rds/ebs/vpc) that achieves the same recall without co-maintaining near-identical fragments in two sibling rules.
evidence: T14 regex (line 120): '(?:\.github/workflows|\bworkflows?\b|workflow_dispatch|pull_request_target|...|\boidc\b|docker-compose|\bcompose\b|...'
Proposed T10 text_all[0]: '\b(?:...|aws|ec2|s3|iam|ssm|...|docker|compose|infra/|...|oidc|\.github/workflows|github actions|workflow_dispatch|pull_request_target|secrets\.[A-Z_]+)\b'
Both entries live in the same _DET_OVERLAY_RULES dict in det_gate_rules.py

The plan states the T10 regex is 'transcribed verbatim from the audit' — confirm whether the audit intentionally duplicated T14 vocabulary or whether a tighter T10-specific vocabulary (terraform/cloudformation/pulumi/ansible/kubernetes/helm/iac/aws/ec2/s3/iam/ssm/rds/ebs/vpc/provision/systemd/user_data) would give equivalent recall with zero overlap
findings.finding: The proposed T10 DET gate regex duplicates substantial vocabulary already present in T14's regex in the same _DET_OVERLAY_RULES dict: '.github/workflows', 'workflow_dispatch', 'pull_request_target', 'oidc', 'docker-compose', 'compose', 'github actions', and 'secrets\.[A-Z_]+' appear verbatim in both. While T10 and T14 serve different criteria (infra applicability vs. CI trigger gaps), placing near-identical trigger fragments in two sibling entries of the same module is a config-surface maintenance burden — a future editor may update one regex without realising the other needs the same change, or may accidentally add T10 terms that fire only because T14's vocabulary is already present in the plan text.
scenarios: A plan touching .github/workflows for a non-infra reason fires T10 via the GHA overlap terms, causing a spurious AGENT-tier T10 invocation (which the LLM router should then PASS not-applicable — cheap, but the gate's stated purpose is to save that cost).
A maintainer updating the T14 regex sees 'oidc' and adds a new OIDC variant without noticing T10 also needs it, causing T10 to miss plans using the new syntax.
